function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

### Quick‑Start Checklist | Step | What to do | Why it matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1️⃣ Clarify Scope** | • Target language(s) (e.g., Russian, English, Arabic)
• Audience (students, scholars, general public)
• Use‑case (FAQ bot, tutoring, research assistant)
• Deployment (cloud, on‑prem, mobile) | Determines data needs, model size, and infrastructure. | | **2️⃣ Choose a Base Model** | • Open‑source (LLaMA‑2, GPT‑NeoX, Mistral, Falcon)
• Proprietary (OpenAI GPT‑4, Anthropic Claude)
• Fine‑tune vs. prompt‑engineering | Balances cost, performance, and control over content. | | **3️⃣ Gather & Clean Data** | • Quranic text, Hadith collections, Tafsir, scholarly articles
• FAQs from reputable Islamic institutions
• Conversational logs (if available)
• Remove duplicates, correct OCR errors, standardize formatting | High‑quality, domain‑specific data improves relevance and reduces hallucinations. | | **4️⃣ Fine‑Tune (or Prompt‑Engineer)** | • Use LoRA or full‑fine‑tune depending on compute
• Add instruction‑style prompts (“Explain the concept of *Sunnah* …”) | Tailors the model’s style and knowledge to your domain. | | **5️⃣ Safety & Bias Mitigation** | • Filter extremist or hateful content
• Add “safe completion” prompts (“I’m sorry, I can’t help with that.”)
• Monitor for misinterpretations or misrepresentations | Protects users and maintains credibility. | | **6️⃣ Evaluate** | • Automatic metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, perplexity)
• Human evaluation (subject matter experts rating accuracy & tone)
• Stress tests (edge‑case questions, ambiguous phrasing) | Ensures the model meets quality standards before release. | | **7️⃣ Deploy & Monitor** | • REST API (FastAPI + Uvicorn)
• Containerization (Docker, Kubernetes)
• Logging & analytics (ELK stack, Prometheus)
• Feedback loop for continuous improvement | Keeps the system reliable, scalable, and responsive to real‑world usage. | --- ## 1️⃣ Clarify Your Project Requirements Before diving into code, answer these questions: | Question | Why it matters | |----------|----------------| | **Target language(s)** | Determines tokenization, vocabulary, and potential multilingual fine‑tuning. | | **Desired model size** | Larger models (13B–70B) give better nuance but require more GPU memory and cost. | | **Compute resources** | Cloud GPUs (A100, H100), local GPU clusters, or TPU pods influence training strategy. | | **Fine‑tune vs. prompt‑engineer** | Fine‑tuning gives deeper domain knowledge; prompt‑engineering is cheaper but less robust. | | **Deployment environment** | Cloud (AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI), on‑prem, or edge devices. | | **Compliance & Ethics** | Must adhere to local laws, religious sensitivities, and OpenAI policy. | | **Budget & Timeline** | Influences choice of model, training duration, and infrastructure. | Feel free to share your answers—this will let me tailor the next steps precisely to your situation. --- ## 2️⃣ Choosing a Base Model | Option | Pros | Cons | Typical Use‑Case | |--------|------|------|------------------| | **Open‑source (LLaMA‑2, Mistral, Falcon)** | Free, full control, can run locally | Requires GPU, licensing may restrict commercial use | Research, internal tooling | | **OpenAI GPT‑4 / Claude** | State‑of‑the‑art, no training needed | API cost, limited customization | Rapid prototyping, low‑maintenance | | **Hybrid (Fine‑tune LLaMA‑2 with LoRA)** | Balance between cost and control | Still needs GPU, LoRA may limit depth | Production chatbot with domain expertise | If you’re on a tight budget or need full control, start with an open‑source model and fine‑tune it. If you want quick results and don’t mind paying per request, GPT‑4 or Claude is a solid choice. --- ## 3️⃣ Data Collection & Preprocessing ### 3.1 Sources | Source | Description | Licensing | |--------|-------------|-----------| | **Quranic Text** | Full Arabic text + translations | Public domain (many translations) | | **Hadith Collections** | Sahih Bukhari, Muslim, etc. | Public domain or Creative Commons | | **Tafsir** | Classical commentaries (e.g., Ibn Kathir) | Varies; many are public domain | | **Islamic FAQ Sites** | e.g., islamqa.info, muslimmatters.org | Usually CC‑BY or public domain | | **Academic Papers** | Articles on Islamic studies | Open access or institutional access | | **Chat Logs** | If you have a legacy chatbot | Must anonymize personal data | ### 3.2 Cleaning Pipeline ```python import re import unicodedata from pathlib import Path def clean_text(text: str) -> str: # Normalize Unicode text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text) # Remove excessive whitespace text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text) # Strip leading/trailing punctuation text = text.strip() return text def load_and_clean(file_path: Path) -> list[str]: with file_path.open(encoding="utf-8") as f: lines = f.readlines() cleaned = [clean_text(line) for line in lines if line.strip()] return cleaned ``` - **Deduplicate**: Use `set()` or `dedupe` library. - **Tokenize**: Use the tokenizer of your chosen base model (`transformers.AutoTokenizer`). - **Chunking**: Split long passages into 512‑token chunks with overlap for context. --- ## 4️⃣ Fine‑Tuning Strategy ### 4.1 Full Fine‑Tune (Large GPU) ```bash accelerate launch train.py \ --model_name_or_path "meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf" \ --dataset_path "/data/islamic_faq" \ --output_dir "/models/llama2-islam-finetuned" \ --per_device_train_batch_size 4 \ --gradient_accumulation_steps 8 \ --learning_rate 2e-5 \ --num_train_epochs 3 ``` - **Pros**: Deep domain adaptation. - **Cons**: Requires 40+ GB GPU memory (A100). ### 4.2 LoRA (Low‑Rank Adaptation) ```bash accelerate launch lora_train.py \ --base_model "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf" \ --dataset_path "/data/islamic_faq" \ --output_dir "/models/lora-llama2-islam" \ --lora_rank 8 \ --train_batch_size 16 \ --learning_rate 1e-4 \ --epochs 5 ``` - **Pros**: Only 1–2 GB GPU memory, fast, cheap. - **Cons**: Slightly less expressive than full fine‑tune. ### 4.3 Prompt‑Engineering (No Training) ```python from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, pipeline tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("openai-community/gpt-4o-mini") model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("openai-community/gpt-4o-mini") prompt_template = """ You are an expert scholar of Islam. Answer the following question in a respectful, concise manner. If you do not know the answer, say "I’m sorry, I don’t have that information." Question: {question} Answer: """ def ask(question: str) -> str: prompt = prompt_template.format(question=question) inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt") outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256) return tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True) ``` - **Pros**: Zero training cost, instant deployment. - **Cons**: Limited control over style and factual accuracy. --- ## 5️⃣ Safety & Bias Mitigation | Technique | Implementation | |-----------|----------------| | **Content Filtering** | Use a blacklist of extremist keywords; drop or rewrite responses containing them. | | **Safe Completion Prompt** | Append “I’m sorry, I can’t help with that.” for disallowed queries. | | **Human‑in‑the‑Loop** | Flag uncertain answers for expert review. | | **Bias Audits** | Run a test set of sensitive questions; measure variance across demographic groups. | | **Version Control** | Keep a changelog of model updates and safety patches. | **Tip:** Use the `datasets` library to create a “bias audit” dataset with questions about gender, ethnicity, and sectarian topics. --- ## 6️⃣ Evaluation ### 6.1 Automatic Metrics ```python from datasets import load_metric bleu = load_metric("bleu") rouge = load_metric("rouge") predictions = ["Answer text"] references = [["Correct answer"]] bleu.add_batch(predictions=predictions, references=references) print(bleu.compute()) ``` ### 6.2 Human Evaluation - Recruit scholars or knowledgeable volunteers. - Rate each answer on **accuracy**, **tone**, **clarity**, **relevance** (scale 1–5). - Use a spreadsheet or a simple web form for feedback. ### 6.3 Stress Tests - Ask ambiguous or trick questions (e.g., “Is *Jihad* always violent?”). - Verify that the model deflects or provides balanced explanations. --- ## 7️⃣ Deployment ### 7.1 API Layer ```python from fastapi import FastAPI, Request from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, pipeline app = FastAPI() tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("/models/llama2-islam-finetuned") model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("/models/llama2-islam-finetuned") @app.post("/ask") async def ask(request: Request): data = await request.json() question = data.get("question", "") inputs = tokenizer(question, return_tensors="pt") outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256) answer = tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True) return {"answer": answer} ``` - **Containerize**: Dockerfile with `FROM python:3.10-slim`. - **Scale**: Deploy on Kubernetes with autoscaling based on CPU/GPU usage. - **Monitoring**: Log latency, error rates, and user feedback. ### 7.2 Front‑End - Simple React or Vue app with a chat UI. - Use WebSocket for real‑time streaming responses. - Store conversation history in a database (PostgreSQL, MongoDB). --- ## 8️⃣ Continuous Improvement Loop 1. **Collect User Feedback** – Store flagged responses. 2. **Curate New Data** – Add new FAQs, scholarly corrections. 3. **Retrain** – Periodically fine‑tune or update LoRA adapters. 4. **Re‑evaluate** – Run automated tests and human audits. 5. **Deploy** – Roll out new model version with A/B testing. --- ## 9️⃣ Resources & References | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | **Hugging Face Model Hub** | https://huggingface.co/models | | **Hugging Face Datasets** | https://huggingface.co/datasets | | **LoRA Tutorial** | https://github.com/microsoft/LoRA | | **OpenAI API Docs** | https://platform.openai.com/docs | | **Islamic Text Corpora** | https://github.com/IslamicTextCorpus | | **Ethics Guidelines** | https://platform.openai.com/docs/policies/usage-policies | --- ### Next Steps 1. **Answer the clarification questions** so I can give you a concrete plan. 2. If you’re ready, I can walk you through setting up a minimal fine‑tune script or a prompt‑engineering prototype. 3. Once you have a prototype, we’ll discuss evaluation and deployment details. Let me know how you’d like to proceed!
